==Problem==
Danica wants to arrange her model cars in rows with exactly 6 cars in each row. She now has 23 model cars. What is the smallest number of additional cars she must buy in order to be able to arrange all her cars this way?

<imath>\textbf{(A)}\ 1 \qquad \textbf{(B)}\ 2 \qquad \textbf{(C)}\ 3 \qquad \textbf{(D)}\ 4 \qquad \textbf{(E)}\ 5</imath>

==Solution 1==
Since each row will have <imath>6</imath> cars, Danica should find the smallest multiple of <imath>6</imath> that is greater than <imath>23</imath> and find the difference between <imath>23</imath> and that number.

We can see that <imath>6 \times 3 = 18 < 23</imath>, but <imath>6 \times 4 = 24 > 23</imath>. This is <imath>1</imath> more than <imath>23</imath>, so the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ 1}</imath>.

~Knittingfrenzy18, modified by anabel.disher, Megaboy6679, and avamarora
